prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Conservative Party Manifesto 2015 – Summary (ideological framing retained)

Core mission: Build a country that rewards hard work, supports aspiration at every stage of life, protects the vulnerable, and keeps Britain secure—anchored by a strong economy and disciplined public finances.

Economy and tax
- Finish the job: eliminate the deficit, then run a surplus to pay down debt—so taxes and mortgage rates stay lower.
- No rises in VAT, Income Tax or National Insurance; crack down on evasion/avoidance.
- Cut Income Tax for 30 million: raise Personal Allowance to £12,500; lift 40p threshold to £50,000; create a Tax‑Free Minimum Wage link.
- Rebalance growth: Northern Powerhouse; metro mayors; major regional transport and science investment.

Jobs, enterprise and skills
- Full employment: help create two million more jobs and three million more apprenticeships; abolish long‑term youth unemployment with stronger work requirements and a new Youth Allowance.
- Best place to do business: competitive business taxes, a major business rates review, £10bn further red‑tape cuts, Start Up Loans trebled, export push, science and technology leadership.

Welfare that works
- Make work pay: lower the household benefit cap to £23,000; roll out Universal Credit; freeze working‑age benefits for two years (with key exemptions).
- Childcare: 30 hours free for working parents of 3–4s; tax‑free childcare.

Health and care
- NHS protected and improved: at least £8bn extra by 2020; a truly 7‑day NHS and GP access; named GP; full transparency and safer care.
- Integrate health and social care via the Better Care Fund; lead on cancer, mental health parity, and dementia.

Education and opportunity
- Guarantee a good primary place; zero tolerance of failure; tougher literacy/numeracy; core academic GCSEs.
- Turn failing/coasting schools into academies; open 500 more free schools; protect per‑pupil funding; expand high‑quality vocational routes and degree apprenticeships; no cap on university places.

Homes and ownership
- Double first‑time buyers; extend Help to Buy; new Help to Buy ISA.
- Build 200,000 Starter Homes (20% discount for under‑40s); 275,000 more affordable homes; extend Right to Buy to Housing Association tenants.
- Prioritise brownfield; protect the Green Belt.

Controlled immigration
- Keep net migration to the tens of thousands by reforming EU welfare rules (four‑year contribution before tax credits/social housing; no benefits for EU jobseekers) and tightening enforcement against abuse and illegal working; fluent‑English requirement in public‑facing roles.

Infrastructure and connectivity
- Record rail and road investment (HS2/HS3, Northern Hub), real‑terms freeze of regulated commuter fares, smart ticketing; superfast broadband to 95% by 2017; stronger mobile coverage and 5G leadership.

Energy and environment
- Keep bills low through competition and smart meters; insulate one million more homes.
- Secure supplies: new nuclear and gas; support shale with a Northern Sovereign Wealth Fund; end new subsidies for onshore wind; meet climate goals cost‑effectively.
- Protect nature: Blue Belt of marine reserves; 11m more trees; keep forests in trust; stronger flood defences.

Law, liberty and security
- Finish police reform; modernise sentencing and prisons; a new Victims’ Law; ban “legal highs.”
- Scrap the Human Rights Act and introduce a British Bill of Rights; stronger counter‑terrorism and anti‑extremism powers.

Strong Union, real devolution, and EU reform
- English votes for English laws; implement new powers for Scotland and Wales; uphold the Northern Ireland settlement.
- EU: renegotiate and hold an in‑out referendum by end‑2017; keep the pound; reclaim powers; expand free trade while protecting the City.

Retirement dignity
- Keep the triple lock; introduce the single‑tier pension; sustain pensioner benefits; cap care costs; free pension freedoms; lift family homes out of Inheritance Tax up to £1m.

Culture, sport, and Big Society
- Free entry to national museums; back creative industries; freeze BBC licence fee pending Charter review.
- Guarantee a place on National Citizen Service; three days’ paid volunteering leave in large firms/public sector; champion equal rights.

Defence and global leadership
- Maintain strong, modern Armed Forces; renew Trident; invest in equipment; support veterans and families.
- Keep 0.7% aid target to save lives, promote stability, and advance UK interests.

Belief in Britain: with discipline, aspiration, and security, we will secure a better future for you, your family, and our country.
